H1: We predict religious affiliation (Religion_type) (categorical IV) will predict time spent living in country of birth (Country_live_time) (continuous DV).

H2: We predict casual sexual experiences and preferences (composite continuous IV; mean of soi_behave, soi_attitude, and soi_desire) will predict relationship duration (Relationship_length) (continuous DV).

(John's code that was done during section is at the very end, below where I added __________)


## 1. Load the package and data
```{r load, message=FALSE}
library(codebook)

#load data/raw/data_doctored.csv
raw <- read.csv("data/raw/data_doctored.csv")

dim(raw)
str(raw)

#get variables for H1 & H2
data <- raw[, c("ResponseId", "Religion_type", "Country_live_time", "Relationship_status", "Relationship_length", 
                "soi_behave", "soi_attitude", "soi_desire")]

dim(raw)
str(raw)
```

## 2. Check participant IDs
```{r participant_ids}

## 2. Check participant IDs
#may be redundant but also trying to follow how John did this during section
summary(data$ResponseId)

#count na 
#counts na in response ID (by taking the sum)
sum(is.na(data$ResponseId))

#count blank
#this is excluding na values (the true part of the function)
sum(data$ResponseId == "", na.rm = TRUE)

#count duplicates
sum(duplicated(data$ResponseId))

#inspect records with missing or blank IDs
missingID <- which(is.na(data$ResponseId))
data[missingID, ]
print(data[missingID, ])

#remove the known empty record with no ID, then check the row count
data <- data[!is.na(data$ResponseId),]

#verify removal of row after running this code by putting dim(data) in terminal
```

## 3. Recode Religious Affiliation
```{r Religion_type}
# codebook: 1 = Christianity, 2 = Islam, 3 = Hinduism, 4 = Buddhism, 5 = Other, 6 = Judaism, 7 = None
table(data$Religion_type, useNA = "ifany")

#turn Religion_type into a factor with labels
data$Religion_type <- factor(data$Religion_type, levels = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7),
                             labels = c("Christianity", "Islam", "Hinduism", "Buddhism", "Other", "Judaism", "None"))
#rerun this to see the update of the names (which succesfully turned into a factor)
table(data$Religion_type, useNA = "ifany")
```


## 4. Validate Time Living in Country of Birth
```{r Country_live_time}
#from the codebook --> Country_live_time is measured in years. Valid responses are 1-80
summary(data$Country_live_time)

#count NAs
sum(is.na(data$Country_live_time))

#count responses outside 1-80
sum(!data$Country_live_time %in% 1:80 & !is.na(data$Country_live_time))

#define LiveTimeValid: Time present & within 1-80
data$LiveTimeValid <- !is.na(data$Country_live_time) & data$Country_live_time %in% 1:80

#check with table below
table(data$LiveTimeValid)

#make h1Data with ID, Religion_Type, and Country_live_time
h1Data <- data[data$LiveTimeValid & !is.na(data$Religion_type), 
               c("ResponseId", "Religion_type", "Country_live_time")]
```

## 5. SOI & Relationship Duration
```{r SOI & Relationship Duration}
#make relData for respondents currently in a relationship
#include Dating (1), In a committed relationship (2), & married (3)
table(data$Relationship_status, useNA = "ifany")
relData <- data[data$Relationship_status %in% c(1, 2, 3), ]

#define the items to check; all three use response codes 1-9
#soi_behave, soi_attitude, and soi_desire: higher codes indicate more unrestricted sociosexuality 
soi_vars <- c("soi_behave", "soi_attitude", "soi_desire")

#check the summaries and missing responses
summary(relData[, soi_vars])
colSums(is.na(relData[, soi_vars]))

#inspect the response frequencies for eeach item
for(i in soi_vars) {
  print(i)
  print(table(relData[, i], useNA = "ifany"))
}

#replace anything outside 1 through 9 with NA
for (i in soi_vars) {
  relData[, i] <- ifelse(relData[, i] %in% 1:9, relData[, i], NA)
}
```

## 6. Calculate SOI composite 
```{r SOI Composite}
#group variables
comVars <- c("soi_behave", "soi_attitude", "soi_desire")

#calculate the composite as the mean of all 3 variables
relData$soiComposite <- rowMeans(relData [, comVars], na.rm = TRUE)

#check score
summary(relData$soiComposite)

#check relationship length (codebook values are 1-80)
summary(relData$Relationship_length)
sum(is.na(relData$Relationship_length))

#count values out of 1-80
summary(!relData$Relationship_length %in% 1:80 & !is.na(relData$Relationship_length))

#make h2Data with ID, SOI composite, and relationship length
#keep participants with SOI composite and valid relationship length
#do not apply the H1 residence-time filter to this hypothesis 
h2Data <- relData [!is.na(relData$soiComposite) & relData$Relationship_length %in% 1:80,
                   c("ResponseId", "soiComposite", "Relationship_length")]
```

## 7. Check the final tables
```{r final_tables}
#check rows, columns, types, and missing values in h1Data
#one row per participant, one column per variable
dim(h1Data)
str(h1Data)
head(h1Data)
colSums(is.na(h1Data))
table(h1Data$Sex_birth,useNA="ifany")
range(h1Data$preference_imp_physat)
sum(duplicated(h1Data$ResponseId))

#repeat the checks for h2Data; both scores should be within 1-7
dim(h2Data)
str(h2Data)
head(h2Data)
colSums(is.na(h2Data))
range(h2Data$qoa)
range(h2Data$commitment)
sum(duplicated(h2Data$ResponseId))
```

## 8. Add labels and generate codebooks
```{r variable_labels}
#add a description to each h1Data column, in column order
#include the source codes, meaning, and units
var_label(h1Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "Religious affiliation: original codes 1 = Christianity, 2 = Islam, 3 = Hinduism, 4 = Buddhism, 5 = other, 6 = Judaism, 7 = None; 
  now stored as a factor",
  "Time spent living in country of birth (Country_live_time); 1-80 years "
)

#add a description to each h2Data column, in column order
#include response anchors and the commitment scoring rule
var_label(h2Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "Casual sexual experiences and preferences: mean of available soi_behave, soi_attitude, and soi_desire responses (each 1-9); 
  no reverse coding; at least one valid response required",
  "Length of current relationship (Relationship_length): years; 1 = one year or less, 2 = 79 corresponding years, 80-80 years or more"
)

#generate the h1Data codebook
compact_codebook(h1Data)


#generate the h2Data codebook
compact_codebook(h2Data)
```

## 9. Save the final tables
```{r save}
#create data/processed_data if needed
dir.create("data/processed_data",recursive=T,showWarnings=F)

#save h1Data and h2Data without an extra row-number column
write.csv(h1Data,"data/processed_data/practice_h1.csv",row.names=F)
write.csv(h2Data,"data/processed_data/practice_h2.csv",row.names=F)

#read the files back and confirm their dimensions
h1Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/practice_h1.csv")
h2Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/practice_h2.csv")
dim(h1Saved)
dim(h2Saved)
```



___________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
John's Hypothesis below:

H1: Points allocated to a partner's physical attractiveness differ by sex at birth.

H2: Confidence in finding a new partner is associated with relationship commitment.

## 1. Load the package and data

```{r load, message=FALSE}
#load the codebook package
library(codebook)

#load data/raw/data_doctored.csv
raw <- read.csv("data/raw/data_doctored.csv")

#check row and column counts, and inspect the first few rows
dim(raw) #shows rows first, followed by columns. In this case should be 117294 rows, 273 columns
#head(raw[, c("ResponseId")]) 
str(raw)


#make data with ID, sex at birth, relationship status, all six preference items, qoa, and prqc_4-6; keep raw unchanged
data <- raw[, c("ResponseId", "Sex_birth", "Relationship_status", "preference_imp_health", "preference_imp_kind", 
                "preference_imp_physat", "preference_imp_relig", "preference_imp_financ", "preference_imp_age", 
                "qoa", "prqc_4", "prqc_5", "prqc_6")]

dim(data)
str(data)

```


## 2. Check participant IDs

```{r participant_ids}

#all of this below can basically just do with this line of code
#summary(data$ResponseId)


#count na 
#counts na in response ID (by taking the sum)
sum(is.na(data$ResponseId))

#count blank
#this is excluding na values (the true part of the function)
sum(data$ResponseId == "", na.rm = TRUE)

#count duplicates
sum(duplicated(data$ResponseId))

#inspect records with missing or blank IDs
missingID <- which(is.na(data$ResponseId))
data[missingID, ]
print(data[missingID, ])

#remove the known empty record with no ID, then check the row count
data <- data[!is.na(data$ResponseId),]
#verify removal of row after running this code by putting dim(data) in terminal

```


## 3. Recode sex at birth

```{r sex_at_birth}
# codebook: 0 = Male, 1 = Female, 2 = Intersex
table(data$Sex_birth, useNA = "ifany")

#turn Sex_birth into a factor with labels Male, Female, and Intersex
data$Sex_birth <- factor(data$Sex_birth, levels = c(0, 1, 2), labels = c("male", "female", "intersex"))

#rerun this to see the update of the names (which successfully turned into a factor)
table(data$Sex_birth, useNA = "ifany")

```


## 4. Validate relative preference

```{r preference_vars}
#group all six preference_imp_ variables
prefvars <- c("preference_imp_health", "preference_imp_kind", 
                "preference_imp_physat", "preference_imp_relig", "preference_imp_financ", "preference_imp_age")


#see summary of variables
summary(data [, prefvars])

#count NAs
colSums(is.na(data[prefvars]))

#calculate total score; leave the total NA if any item is missing
data$prefTotal <- rowSums(data[, prefvars], na.rm = FALSE)
#check by using summary function
summary(data$prefTotal)

#count those that do not sum to 30
sum(data$prefTotal != 30 & !is.na(data$prefTotal))

#check that each observed allocation is between 0 and 30
data$prefRange <- rowSums(data [, prefvars] < 0 | data[, prefvars] > 30, na.rm = TRUE) == FALSE



#define prefValid: total present, total equals 30, and each item in range
data$prefvalid <- !is.na(data$prefTotal) & data$prefTotal == 30 & data$prefRange
#check with table below
table(data$prefvalid)

#make h1Data with ID, Sex_birth, and preference_imp_physat
h1Data <- data[data$prefvalid & !is.na(data$Sex_birth), c("ResponseId", "Sex_birth", "preference_imp_physat")]

```


## 5. qoa & commitment
```{r qoa_commitment}
#make relData for respondents currently in a relationship
#include Dating (1), In a committed relationship (2), and Married (3)
table(data$Relationship_status, useNA = "ifany")
relData <- data[data$Relationship_status %in% c(1, 2, 3), ]


#define the items to check; all four use response codes 1-7
#qoa: 1=Strongly disagree, 7=Strongly agree
#prqc_4-6: 1=Not at all, 7=Extremely
likert7 <- c("qoa", "prqc_4", "prqc_5", "prqc_6")

#check the summaries and missing responses
summary(relData [, likert7])
colSums(is.na(relData[, likert7]))


#inspect the response frequencies for each item
for(i in likert7) {
  print(i)
  print(table(relData[, i], useNA = "ifany"))
}




#replace any codes outside 1-7 with NA
for(i in likert7) {
  relData[, i] <- ifelse(relData[, i] %in% 1:7, relData[, i], NA)
}

```

## 6. Calculate commitment

```{r commitment}
#group commitment variables (prqc_4, prqc_5, and prqc_6)
#these ask how committed, dedicated, and devoted respondents are
#none requires reverse coding
comVars <- c("prqc_4", "prqc_5", "prqc_6")


#calculate commitment as the mean of all three items
#for NAs, conduct available item mean
relData$commitment <- rowMeans(relData[, comVars], na.rm = TRUE)

#check the score
summary(relData$commitment)

#make h2Data with ID, qoa, and commitment
#keep participants with both qoa and commitment present
#do not apply the H1 preference filter to this hypothesis
h2Data <- relData[ !is.na(relData$qoa) & !is.na(relData$commitment), c("ResponseId", "qoa", "commitment")]

```

## 7. Check the final tables

```{r final_tables}
#check rows, columns, types, and missing values in h1Data
#one row per participant, one column per variable
dim(h1Data)
str(h1Data)
head(h1Data)
colSums(is.na(h1Data))
table(h1Data$Sex_birth,useNA="ifany")
range(h1Data$preference_imp_physat)
sum(duplicated(h1Data$ResponseId))

#repeat the checks for h2Data; both scores should be within 1-7
dim(h2Data)
str(h2Data)
head(h2Data)
colSums(is.na(h2Data))
range(h2Data$qoa)
range(h2Data$commitment)
sum(duplicated(h2Data$ResponseId))
```

## 8. Add labels and generate codebooks

The descriptions come from the original codebook and our scoring decisions.
`compact_codebook()` adds summaries from the actual data. Knit the Rmd to
display the formatted codebooks.

```{r variable_labels}
#add a description to each h1Data column, in column order
#include the source codes, meaning, and units
var_label(h1Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "Sex at birth: original codes 0=Male, 1=Female, 2=Intersex; now stored as a factor",
  "Points allocated to partner physical attractiveness; 0-30 points from a 30-point budget; zero is valid"
)

#add a description to each h2Data column, in column order
#include response anchors and the commitment scoring rule
var_label(h2Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "Confidence in finding another appealing partner if the current relationship ended; 1=Strongly disagree, 7=Strongly agree",
  "Relationship commitment: mean of available prqc_4-6 responses, each 1=Not at all to 7=Extremely; no reverse coding; at least one valid response required"
)

```

H1 includes participants with an ID, a valid sex-at-birth category, and six
allocations between 0 and 30 that total 30. Factor level numbers in the
generated table are internal R positions, not the original survey codes.

```{r h1_codebook}
#generate the h1Data codebook
compact_codebook(h1Data)

```

H2 includes participants with an ID, relationship status 1, 2, or 3, and
valid nonmissing qoa and at least one valid commitment response.

```{r h2_codebook}
#generate the h2Data codebook
compact_codebook(h2Data)

```

## 9. Save the final tables

```{r save}
#create data/processed_data if needed
dir.create("data/processed_data",recursive=T,showWarnings=F)

#save h1Data and h2Data without an extra row-number column
write.csv(h1Data,"data/processed_data/practice_h1.csv",row.names=F)
write.csv(h2Data,"data/processed_data/practice_h2.csv",row.names=F)

#read the files back and confirm their dimensions
h1Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/practice_h1.csv")
h2Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/practice_h2.csv")
dim(h1Saved)
dim(h2Saved)

```
